audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Darius / Darius / Skill / Darius / Skill / Darius / Darius while whys[2] says 'Level 3 favours Darius', whys[3] says 'Levels 4-5 favour Wukong' and whys[6] says 'Two-plus items are a skill matchup'. Three cells contradict the sentence beside them, and the Levels 4-5 cell inverts it — the chart hands Darius the exact stage the entry calls Wukong's spike.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster is 22s at rank 1 and is the answer to Apprehend; the stage where Wukong first has it is the stage he wins, and the chart currently says the opposite. The packet chart (Darius, Darius, Darius, Wukong, Wukong, Darius, Skill) agrees with whys[0]-[3], whys[5] and whys[6] at a 49.1% win rate over 3831 games.
audit.corrected: win[2] to Darius, win[3] to Wukong, win[6] to Skill in both layers as one group with ratings realigned. Level 6 left at Skill: the packet says Wukong and whys[4] says Darius, and Cyclone interrupting the Guillotine cast against a baited clone genuinely cuts both ways — whys[4] rewritten to say 'even' so the prose stops arguing with the cell.
sources: internal contradiction with whys[2], whys[3], whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase text carries the LaTeX fragment 'R = d + a \times Stacks'. Wukong's spikes are listed as 'Nimbus Strike online, level 6, first item' with no cooldown given anywhere, and the entry repeatedly calls the clone 'a long CD' without saying how long.
audit.why: The numbers are the advice here: Warrior Trickster 22s falling to 18s is the entire window you play around, Nimbus Strike 10s to 7s, Crushing Blow 8s to 6s, Cyclone 130/110/90. 'Long CD' is unactionable when Apprehend's own 26s is longer than the clone's at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Plain-language Level 6 text plus real cooldowns in phases, spikes, dos/don'ts, breakdown.cooldowns and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The armour shred is credited to E in six places — spikes[0] 'his E gap-close plus armor-shred', spikes[2] 'his early E-shred spike', wants.foe[1] 'E gap-close plus armor shred', whys[3] 'E-shred wins trades', whys[5] and content.mid 'his faded E-shred'. The full layer also calls Nimbus Strike 'His escape from your pull' and tracks it as the matchup-defining ability. Stone Skin is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text: Crushing Blow (Q) is the one that 'reduces the target's armor'; Nimbus Strike (E) 'dashes to a targeted enemy and sends out images' — it is a gap-closer toward a target, so it only functions as an escape if there is a minion to leave on. The ability that actually beats Apprehend is Warrior Trickster: 'Wukong becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone'. And Stone Skin gives him 'stacking armor and max health regeneration while fighting champions' — which matters twice over here, because Apprehend passively ignores a percentage of his armour and Noxian Guillotine is true damage, so neither is blunted by it.
audit.corrected: Armour shred attributed to Crushing Blow throughout, Nimbus Strike restated as a gap-closer needing a target, the tracked ability moved to Warrior Trickster, and Stone Skin named against Apprehend's armour penetration and Guillotine's true damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns is a PDF-extraction run-on ending in the page artefact '• • Darius Top Lane Matchup Database 33', names the wrong ability as matchup-defining and gives Apprehend only 'Long early cooldown'.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster's 22s is the window the whole lane turns on, and Apprehend at 26s at rank 1 is longer than it — a fact the player needs and the block never states.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the real cooldowns, correct matchup-defining ability and the artefact removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says Nimbus Strike needs a target to travel to, and nothing says the clone attacks on its own.
audit.why: Both are in Riot's text and both change play: deny him a stray minion and his cheap dash cannot take him anywhere, and the clone 'will attack nearby enemies', so the thing hitting you is not proof you found the real one.
